annotation_notes: For CS320 - Software Engineering, replace prerequisite CS101 with MATH220 - Linear Algebra. The DIRECT edit swaps chain element 0 CS101 -> MATH220. Because this plan lists transitive prerequisite chains (e.g. CS301 = [CS201, CS101]) and master_data supplies MATH220's chain [MATH101 - Calculus I], MATH101 is pulled into CS320's chain as a CASCADE (add). eligibility_rule: eligible iff every chain course is in completed_courses [CS101, MATH101]; MATH220 is not completed, so eligible true -> false (cascade). eligibility_summary currently_eligible 4 -> 3, currently_ineligible 8 -> 9 (cascade; total_planned 12 unchanged). Only CS320 re-derives; courses depending on CS320 stay ineligible. | REVIEW EDIT (with author): the prerequisite edit was re-annotated during review. (1) The new chain was restored to the transitive [MATH220 - Linear Algebra, MATH101 - Calculus I] (not the literal one-for-one [MATH220]), because this plan lists transitive chains (CS301 = [CS201, CS101]) and master_data supplies MATH220 prereq chain [MATH101], so the convention-consistent deterministic value includes MATH101. (2) The edit was split by kind: replace /prerequisite_chain/0 CS101->MATH220 is DIRECT (the requested swap), while add /prerequisite_chain/- MATH101 is CASCADE (the transitive prerequisite pulled in) - the literal swap is the direct edit and the MATH101 propagation is the cascade, scored separately.
conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a course list where each planned course's eligibility derives from whether its prerequisite chain is satisfied by a stated set of completed courses, with the eligibility rule stated. Around this core, add the realistic, independent details a course plan would carry that do not depend on the prerequisites, and vary their number and the number of courses from sample to sample.
edit_pattern: Change one course's prerequisite to a different specific course.
cascade_pattern: Changing a course's prerequisite to a new one (whose own prerequisite chain is supplied with the edit instruction) re-derives that course's eligibility from whether the new chain is satisfied by the completed set. Courses with unchanged prerequisites stay. This is determined because the new prerequisite's chain is provided with the edit.
